title: Zarokh, the Temporal: Temple of Chaos Honour, Relics and Boss Entry
summary: How the Temple of Chaos works in Path of Exile 2: Honour as a separate health pool, how Relic Altars and Sacred Water scale your run, room objectives, and the readiness check before fighting Zarokh for Ascendancy points.
description: A complete walkthrough of the Temple of Chaos in Path of Exile 2: Honour mechanics, Relic loadouts, room routing, Affliction risks, and the boss-entry readiness check for Zarokh, the Temporal.
prerequisites: Reach the Temple of Chaos by clearing the Act 3 Trial of Chaos at least once
A mapping character that can comfortably clear T15+ maps
Basic understanding of your build's defences: Honour, life, resistances and recovery
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Zarokh, the Temporal, the final boss of the Temple of Chaos in Path of Exile 2

items.title: What is Zarokh, the Temporal?
body: Zarokh, the Temporal is the final boss of the Temple of Chaos, the repeatable endgame version of the Trial of Chaos. You reach him only after clearing the randomised Chaos rooms on a chosen floor.
Defeating him on floor 3 grants 2 Ascendancy points; progressing to floor 4 and killing him again grants the next 2 points, mirroring the Sekhemas ladder.

items.title: How is the Temple of Chaos different from the campaign trial?
body: The Act 3 Trial of Chaos is a one-time quest gate. The Temple of Chaos is the endgame instance you enter with a Barya, where floors and rooms scale and rewards accumulate across attempts.

items.title: What is Honour and why does it matter?
body: Honour is a separate health pool used only inside the Chaos trial. If Honour reaches zero, the run fails immediately regardless of your life total, so protecting it is the core skill of the encounter.

items.title: Why did I kill the boss but get no Ascendancy points?
body: After Zarokh dies you must click the Ascendancy altar that appears. Leaving the instance without clicking it forfeits the points for that clear.

sections.title: Before you enter
paragraphs: The Temple of Chaos expects a character that already clears T15+ maps. Raw campaign gear will not survive floor 3 Honour pressure.

Make sure your build has consistent damage mitigation and some form of recovery. Honour does not regenerate the same way life does, so sustain comes from Honour Resistance, Maximum Honour and Sacred Water pickups rather than life regeneration.

Bring a Barya that matches the floor you intend to attempt. The first quest Barya is consumed by the tutorial; later runs use standard or higher-tier Baryas that you obtain from the campaign or trade.
bullets: Confirm your resistances and defensive layers are mapped-ready
Decide your target floor (3 for the first 2 points, 4 for the next 2)
Plan whether you will cash out rewards or push deeper before entering

sections.title: Relic loadout priorities
sections.intro: Relics are slotted at the Altar between rooms. Prioritise attributes that keep Honour healthy before damage or greed attributes.

cards.title: Honour Resistance relics
body: The highest-priority slot. Every point reduces Honour damage taken and directly lowers the chance a single Affliction brick ends your run.
Take these before any offensive relic unless your damage is genuinely too low to clear rooms.

cards.title: Maximum Honour relics
body: Adds a buffer on top of resistance. Best when you already have decent resistance but still occasionally get one-shot by layered Afflictions.

cards.title: Sacred Water relics
body: Increase the amount of Honour restored by Sacred Water. Strong when your route includes many Merchant or water nodes.

cards.title: Offence / utility relics
body: Damage, movement or special-effect relics are a luxury. Only slot them once defence and sustain are comfortably covered for your target floor.

sections.title: How Relic slots unlock
paragraphs: The Relic Altar starts with a limited number of sockets. Clearing rooms and reaching certain nodes expands the Altar, letting you carry more relics deeper into the floor.
Each additional socket is a meaningful power spike because it lets you stack a second defensive relic or add sustain without dropping your core resistance relic.
Plan your altar around the floor you intend to finish on. If you only want floor 3 points, a smaller loadout is fine; pushing to floor 4 rewards a fuller, more defensive board.
bullets: Unlock sockets steadily rather than gambling on a single huge relic
Keep at least one resistance relic slotted at all times
Re-evaluate your board after every Merchant visit

sections.title: Choosing your route
paragraphs: The map between rooms shows known nodes, Merchant nodes, reward nodes and unknown nodes. Known safe nodes are almost always better than gambling on an unknown when your Honour is already low.
Favour routes that chain a Merchant or Sacred Water node before any high-risk combat room. Entering a Defeat All room at low Honour is how most runs end.
If your goal is simply the Ascendancy points, the shortest path to the boss with the fewest dangerous rooms is often the correct one; the extra reward rooms are optional.
bullets: Avoid unknown nodes when Honour is low
Shortest safe path beats greedy long routes for points

sections.title: Sacred Water and the Merchant
paragraphs: Sacred Water is the primary in-run Honour recovery. Picking it up during rooms and buying more at the Merchant keeps your effective health pool high for the boss.
The Merchant also sells relics and sometimes rerolls. Spend cautiously: a defensive relic that completes your resistance breakpoint is usually worth more than a small offence upgrade.
Do not skip the Merchant when your Honour is mid-to-low. The cost of a slightly longer route is far lower than the cost of a bricked run.

steps.label: Honour buffer
body: Enter with enough Honour that a single layered hit will not end the run. Top up at the last Merchant if needed.

steps.label: Resistance relic slotted
body: Confirm your primary Honour Resistance relic is still equipped after any rerolls.

steps.label: Sacred Water stocked
body: Buy or pick up water right before the boss room so your Honour is near maximum.

steps.label: Damage check
body: Make sure your damage can actually clear Zarokh's phases; a stalled fight draws out Honour pressure.

steps.label: Altar plan
body: Remember you must click the Ascendancy altar after the kill, or the points are lost.

sections.title: Co-op and platform notes
sections.intro: Honour and revival behave differently depending on group size and platform.

tabs.label: PC
paragraphs: Standard solo or group play. Honour is shared per player; a downed ally costs their Honour contribution for the rest of the room.
bullets: Full control over relic management and routing
Group play splits pressure but shares Honour risk

tabs.label: Console
paragraphs: Same mechanics as PC. Couch co-op shares the instance and Honour pool; coordinate who clicks the altar.
bullets: Confirm the altar click is not missed on split control
Revival rules still drain Honour for the group

sections.title: What players report
sections.intro: Common community experiences. Treat as strategy, not guaranteed mechanics.

cards.title: Resistance breakpoint feels like a wall
body: Many players report the run becomes stable only after a certain Honour Resistance threshold; below it, Afflictions feel random.

cards.title: Water timing matters more than DPS
body: Several clears credited reaching the boss at near-full Honour over having higher damage.

cards.title: Don't skip the altar
body: A frequent mistake is leaving the instance after the kill without clicking the Ascendancy altar, forfeiting the points.

sections.title: Common problems
paragraphs: If Honour keeps hitting zero in early rooms, your resistance relic is too weak or your route is too greedy. Drop an offence relic for defence and take safer known nodes.
If you cleared the boss but got no points, you left without clicking the Ascendancy altar. Re-enter only if the trial allows; otherwise the points are granted on a future successful clear.
If co-op feels harder, remember Honour is shared per player; a downed ally removes their contribution and raises everyone's effective risk.
bullets: Low Honour death = stack resistance, not damage
